events.reason: Severe upper abdominal pain with vomiting

reports.text:
INDICATION: Epigastric pain radiating to the back, elevated lipase.
TECHNIQUE: Real-time grayscale and color Doppler sonography of the right upper quadrant.
FINDINGS: Liver normal in size and echotexture without focal lesion. Gallbladder well distended, no stones or sludge, wall not thickened, no pericholecystic fluid; sonographic Murphy sign negative. Common bile duct 3 mm, not dilated. No intrahepatic biliary dilatation. Visualized pancreatic head unremarkable; body and tail partly obscured by overlying bowel gas. Right kidney normal in size without hydronephrosis. No free fluid in the right upper quadrant.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 03/12/2026. Copy to primary care.

CHIEF COMPLAINT: abdominal pain, vomiting

HPI: 24 yo M, construction worker, presents with severe sharp pain in the upper abdomen going through to the back since early this morning, with nausea and several episodes of emesis. States he has had attacks like this on and off for about three months, not as bad, each lasting a day or so and settling at home; did not seek care for them. This one did not let up. Last alcohol 4 days ago (2-3 drinks/wk at baseline). No fever, no diarrhea, no hematemesis.

PMH (per patient and outside list): hyperzincemia, elevated triglycerides
MEDS: zinc gluconate 50 mg daily, multivitamin daily
ALLERGIES: NKDA
FHx: father HTN; mother migraine; no known inherited metabolic disease
SHx: never smoker; social EtOH; no drug use

EXAM: uncomfortable, lying still. Vitals per flowsheet.
Abd: tender in the epigastrium, no rebound, no guarding, bowel sounds present. No jaundice.
Heart RRR. Lungs clear.

RESULTS: lipase 1800 U/L, amylase 2000 U/L, triglycerides 2000 mg/dL. CBC and CMP otherwise unremarkable.
RUQ US: no gallstones, no biliary obstruction.

ED COURSE: IV fluids started, IV ondansetron and IV hydromorphone with improvement. 

IMPRESSION: Acute pancreatitis, hypertriglyceridemia-induced; gallstones not seen.

DISPOSITION: admitted to the hospitalist service.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (received)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
HOSPITALIST DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/12/2026 via ED. Discharged 03/15/2026 to home.

Principal diagnosis: acute pancreatitis secondary to hypertriglyceridemia, without necrosis or infection.

Brief history: 24 y/o male with known elevated triglycerides presented with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back with vomiting. Lipase 1800, amylase 2000, TG 2000 on arrival. RUQ ultrasound without gallstones or ductal dilatation.

Hospital course: Made NPO with IV lactated Ringer's. IV ondansetron and IV hydromorphone as needed, weaned by day 2. Pain resolved and he was advanced to clear liquids on day 2 and a low-fat diet on day 3, which he tolerated. Triglycerides 640 on the morning of discharge. Started on fenofibrate. Counseled at length to stop alcohol completely and keep to a low-fat diet; he was agreeable.

Discharge medications:
- NEW fenofibrate 145 mg PO daily
- multivitamin 1 tab daily
- zinc gluconate 50 mg daily: patient states he is not taking

Allergies: NKDA

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with fasting lipid panel. Return for recurrent abdominal pain, vomiting or fever.
Work: off until seen by PCP.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transition of care call after discharge 3/15 for pancreatitis. Spoke with patient. Reports he is feeling a lot better, no pain since Saturday, eating small low-fat meals and keeping them down. No vomiting, no fever. Picked up fenofibrate yesterday and took first home dose. Reviewed discharge med list with him: fenofibrate daily, multivitamin; not on zinc. Has not had any alcohol. Booked with PCP Thursday 3/19 at 7:30, fasting for labs. Knows to call or come in sooner for return of pain or vomiting.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up (TCM). ED record and discharge summary reviewed.

August was admitted 3/12-3/15 with acute pancreatitis from hypertriglyceridemia: lipase 1800, amylase 2000, TG 2000 on arrival, no gallstones on ultrasound. Treated with bowel rest and IV fluids; TG 640 at discharge, started on fenofibrate 145 mg.

Today: no abdominal pain since the weekend. Eating normally, has cut out fried food and fast food lunches at work. Taking fenofibrate every morning, no muscle aches. Has had no alcohol since discharge and plans to keep it that way. Off the zinc since September as before. He tells me the attacks over the winter were milder and he just rode them out at home.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Comfortable.
Abdomen soft, nontender including epigastrium, no organomegaly.
No jaundice.

A/P:
1. Acute pancreatitis, resolved clinically.
2. Hypertriglyceridemia, now with pancreatitis. Continue fenofibrate 145 mg daily, low-fat diet, no alcohol. Fasting lipid panel and CMP today. Repeat lipids, liver tests and creatinine in 2 months, then video visit.
3. Work: cleared to return to full duty Monday 3/23. Letter given.

Return sooner for any recurrent pain or vomiting.

documents.title: Return to Work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To whom it may concern:

August Curran was under medical care from March 12 through March 19, 2026. He may return to work without restrictions on Monday, March 23, 2026.

Please contact our office with any questions.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: Labs from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: August, triglycerides are down to 380, from 2000 in the ER and 640 when you left the hospital. Heading the right way. Kidney and liver tests are normal. Keep up the fenofibrate, the diet changes and no alcohol. Next labs in May.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request - fenofibrate
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Pharmacy request to convert fenofibrate 145 mg (30-day supply from hospital discharge) to a 90-day supply under his plan. Pended for PCP.

PCP: approved, 90 days with 3 refills.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home after work, identity confirmed.

Doing well. No abdominal pain since March. Taking fenofibrate daily without side effects. Still not drinking. Packing his own lunches.

Labs 5/18: TG 260 (2000 in March, 380 a week after discharge). Liver tests and creatinine normal.

A/P: hypertriglyceridemia on fenofibrate, improving. Continue fenofibrate 145 mg daily, diet, no alcohol. Fasting lipids with his physical in September.

documents.title: Fill history reviewed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fill notice: fenofibrate 145 mg #90 refilled 7/27, on schedule. No action needed.

documents.title: physical
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Need to book my physical for sometime in september. mornings before 8 are best. do I need to fast again

documents.title: RE: physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi August, you're booked Monday 9/14 at 7:30 AM. Yes, please come fasting so we can draw your lipids that morning.
